newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end ahead on demand for Verbund.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end ahead on demand for Verbund.

text.p: Austrian shares ended with moderate gains on Wednesday and just off session highs thanks to selective interest particularly in Verbund, traders said.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips gained 5.35 points, or 0.41 percent, to 1,304.17 -- a shade off the high at 1,304.66. Of its constituents, 16 shares advanced while five fell.
Traders expect the ATX to remain hinged into a narrow trading range around 1,300 points for the rest of the week.
"I don't expect any great leaps," said one, forecasting a range of 1,290 to 1,310 points.
"We'll continue hovering around 1,300," said another, adding in a worst-case scenario the ATX could fall to 1,260 "but we're sooner headed higher."
The day's best performing stock was Bank Austria's preferred, adding on 1.64 percent to 424 ats, while microchip maker AMS led decliners, losing 0.54 percent to 937.05.
National grid company Verbund was the most actively traded on turnover of 168,524 lots, up 14 schillings at 883 on demand from both abroad and home.
"Verbund was a tough dog for a long time," said a trader, "and now there's this big order in the market."
The broad-based Vienna bourse index added on 0.78 points, or 0.16 percent, to 478.26.
The June ATX future climbed two points to 1,297.5 on turnover of 312 contracts.
